content: based on the actual score, segment by phrase in groups and do an algorithm that allows to transpose the whole phrase using any note of the phrase as a pivot note and setting a target pitch. The pivot note and the target pitch apply for all segments. So, for example, we can use the first note of every segment as a pivot note and set it to E4. This means that all phrases will have their first note at E4. If we set the third note as a pivot note and target pitch at G3, all phrases will transpose their structure so that their third note is G3. If the pivot note is out of range of the group (the pivot note is the 7th note and the phrase has only 6 notes...) the last note is used as pivot.

content:
**Principle.** The score in the roll is segmented into phrases (silence gaps) per voice; each phrase is transposed as a whole so that one chosen note of it lands on the target pitch — all notes shift by the same amount. The pivot is selected per phrase (first, last, highest, lowest, or a fixed index), and when the requested index exceeds the phrase length it falls back to the last note.

**Parameters.**
- `pivot` (menu): which note of each phrase anchors the transposition — first, last, highest, lowest, or a fixed index.
- `index` (slider): the note number used when pivot is "nᵗʰ" (falls back to the last note if out of range).
- `target` (slider, mc): the pitch every pivot lands on.
- `gap` (slider, ms): silence that separates phrases.
